<body style="margin: 0px; padding: 28px; background: var(--gray-50,#FAF9EA); font-family: var(--th-body);">
  <div id="root">
    <div style="display: flex; gap: 40px; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start;">
      <div class="col">
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Default — hug, aligned end"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--end lds-btn-group--stack" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--secondary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save draft"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save changes"
          <div class="dim">
            "Confirming action last in source, so it lands at the end of the reading direction."
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Split — cancel at the opposite end"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--split lds-btn-group--stack" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--tertiary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Cancel"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save changes"
          <div class="dim">
            "Cancel is not a peer of confirm: dismissing and committing become opposite physical directions instead of adjacent targets."
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Conversion — detail outside the button"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--conversion" role="group">
              <div class="lds-btn-group__detail">
                <span class="lds-btn-group__detail-title">
                  "$248 total"
                <span class="lds-btn-group__detail-note">
                  "3 nights · includes fees"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Reserve"
          <div class="dim">
            "A button label is a verb. The price, the count and the qualifier sit to its left, so the target stays one word and the detail has room to be specific."
        <div class="force-mobile">
          <div class="lbl">
            "Conversion under 560px"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--conversion" role="group">
              <div class="lds-btn-group__detail">
                <span class="lds-btn-group__detail-title">
                  "$248 total"
                <span class="lds-btn-group__detail-note">
                  "3 nights · includes fees"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Reserve"
          <div class="dim">
            "The detail stays above the button here, not below it — it is the reason for the tap. Only cancel/confirm pairs reverse on stack."
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Fill — equal shares of the width"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--fill lds-btn-group--end lds-btn-group--stack" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--secondary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save draft"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save changes"
          <div class="dim">
            "For a narrow container or a sheet footer, where hugging leaves the row looking unfinished."
      <div class="col" style="width: 300px;">
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Vertical"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--vertical lds-btn-group--fill lds-btn-group--end" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--secondary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save draft"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save changes"
          <div class="dim">
            "Already a column, so it never stacks."
        <div class="force-mobile">
          <div class="lbl">
            "Under 560px — stacks and fills"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--split lds-btn-group--stack" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--tertiary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Cancel"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Save changes"
          <div class="dim">
            "Reversed on purpose: the confirming action sits at the top of the stack, under the thumb. Pass stackOnMobile={false} to keep a row."
        <div>
          <div class="lbl">
            "Allowed styles"
          <div class="box">
            <div class="lds-btn-group lds-btn-group--split lds-btn-group--stack" role="group">
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--tertiary lds-btn--sm">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Cancel"
              <button class="lds-btn lds-btn--primary lds-btn--sm hue-red">
                <span class="lds-btn__label">
                  "Delete"
          <div class="dim">
            "One primary per group. Secondary for a peer action, tertiary for cancel. Destructive keeps the primary shape and takes the red hue — colour comes from the ramp, never a hex."

There used to be a second: a warm pink-beige ramp shipped as the palette's ninth hue, unrelated to any theme's surfaces. Two spellings, two temperatures, one meaning; it is gone."

"Core's is warm — the portfolio's oat paper, not a true gray — so every theme declares its own: a dashboard on oat renders cream, which is why Product ships a true neutral and Palette and Roadtrip ship cool dark ramps."

"The chroma carries a curve rather than a flat value. It is felt in the light-mid tints, eased through the value mids where text legibility lives, and deepest in the shadows, so a border or a sunken fill sits in a colour instead of in a gray. "The blue was #00437C, Lc 85.6 on oat: technically blue, perceptually navy. It is now #005391 at Lc 79.9 — one step down the contrast curve for a visible step up in blueness. "Prose and display — the reading roles"
"--text-hero" "clamp(44–72px) · 1.0 · Coconat"

"Making the building happen"

"A card title is a thing you act on"

"--text-body" "17px · 1.35 · Ronzino"

"Body is the default reading size, and it is set large on purpose: a 17px measure with settled leading holds a paragraph of real explanation without the reader leaning in. Everything that is prose takes this role — card bodies, banner messages, modal copy — so a page has one reading size rather than four near-misses."

"--text-caption" "15px · --leading-normal"

"Caption is small prose, not metadata. A sentence explaining a field or a footnote under a figure belongs here; a counter or a date does not, because 15px is generous for a number and 12px is too small for a sentence."

"--text-meta" "12px · Martian Mono"

"v1.0.0 · 24 icons · #3EA65D"

"How this sets the density"

"Three families do three jobs." "Prose" "is the larger of the two reading families and settled rather than airy — 17px on 1.35, which holds a paragraph together in the narrow column a card or a modal actually gives it." "Chrome" "sits below it on the same scale — a 14px button beside 17px body is what makes an interface feel like an interface rather than a document." "Meta" "is mono and fixed at 12px, for output a machine produced — the one place that step still belongs."

"The gap between the prose and chrome families is the density dial for the whole system: widen it and the page reads editorial, close it and it reads like a dashboard. Individual components never pick a pixel — they pick a step — so this is one edit, not fifty."

"--density" "scales control text and padding together, per theme. Core ships 1; Product and Roadtrip ship 0.92, which is the same components at dashboard density."
